tldr: The paper proposes Reflect, Retry, Reward, a self-improvement method where LLMs generate self-reflections after task failure, retry with the reflection in context, and use GRPO reinforcement learning to reward tokens from successful self-reflections—without requiring task-specific training data.
contributions: A novel task-agnostic methodology for training LLMs to generate better self-reflections using only binary success/failure feedback from a verifier
Demonstration of substantial performance gains on function calling (APIGen) and math equation writing (Countdown) tasks without synthetic data generation
Showing that smaller fine-tuned models (1.5B–7B) can outperform models in the same family that are up to 10x larger
A multi-step GRPO implementation that rewards only self-reflection tokens while zeroing advantage terms for all other generated tokens
methods: The framework operates in two stages: first, upon failing a task, the model generates a self-reflective commentary analyzing its previous attempt; second, the model retries the task with the self-reflection included in context. If the second attempt succeeds, GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) is used to reward only the tokens generated during the self-reflection phase, with advantage terms for all other tokens set to zero. Training was conducted on failure datasets (only queries where the model initially failed), using up to 1,750 training steps with an effective batch size of 256, KL divergence coefficient of 0.001, and learning rate of 5e-7 with cosine annealing. Experiments were run on 4–8 H100 GPUs for models between 1.5B and 8B parameters.
results: Performance gains of up to 34.7% on math equation writing and 18.1% on function calling were observed. On APIGen, self-reflection increased performance by an average of 4.5% before GRPO training and 4.7% after GRPO training. On Countdown, improvements were 5.3% before and 8.6% after GRPO training. The GRPO-trained Qwen2-7B model outperformed a vanilla Qwen2-72B model when both were given two attempts, despite being 10x smaller. Vanilla model self-reflections tended to be long, confusing, and redundant, while GRPO-finetuned models produced shorter, clearer, and more generalizable reflections. MMLU-Pro, GSM8K, HellaSwag, and MATH benchmark scores showed minimal change between vanilla and trained models.
limitations: Models smaller than 1.5B parameters had very limited capacity for accurate answering and self-reflection and could not be effectively trained. GRPO training has known computational efficiency and scalability concerns, limiting experiments to models between 1.5B and 8B parameters. Some models like Phi 3.5-mini struggled significantly with equation writing despite handling function calling. The approach requires a binary verifier, which for some task types may still need gold-standard target answers. Catastrophic forgetting analysis was limited, with results shown for only a subset of benchmarks.
